title: Austin 911 response time
summary: Retrospective research on whether source-reported 911 response time exceeds 20 minutes, using recorded dispatch context with unverified historical availability.

post.title: A prediction task from Austin's 911 calls
paragraphs: This release turns City of Austin call records into a prediction task with temporal training, evaluation and holdout splits. The construction code, qualification checks and a reproducible baseline travel with the dataset.

The target uses the source's response_time field. The threshold was selected using the training period and then frozen. Prediction time and the outcome's clock are distinct: the source measures response time from the call being answered, while response_datetime records the opening of the call-taker's dispatch screen.
The recorded baseline demonstrates the runner's training and prediction contract on this artifact. It is not an agent or harness comparison.

limitations: This is a derived research dataset, not an official City of Austin product or a recommendation about emergency response.
The source outcome clock and prediction timestamp differ. Read the documented clock-offset measurements before interpreting the target.
The holdout is downloadable. Keep its labels outside the evaluated agent's workspace during an evaluation.
No claim of real-time or operational forecasting validity; historical availability at the prediction instant is assumed, not vintage-verified.

The labeled eval split is development/validation. Final holdout scoring requires prediction-time access restrictions; the original scorer provided the complete feature frame. Downloadable holdout labels must stay outside model development.
